title: What artificial intelligence is revealing about ancient Pompeii
summary:
POMPEII – Artificial intelligence and archaeology are coming together in two new projects at Pompeii, one of the ancient world's most iconic sites.
The second allows visitors to the archaeological site to step virtually inside ancient buildings and experience them as they were 2,000 years ago.
By combining physical anthropological and archaeological evidence with volcanological data, a team from the Pompeii Archaeological Park and the University of Padua, whose Digital Cultural Heritage Laboratory is headed by Jacopo Bonetto, has recreated the escape of one of the victims.
"If used properly, AI can help revitalise classical studies by presenting the ancient world in a more immersive way," explains Gabriel Zuchtriegel, the 45-year-old director of the Pompeii Archaeological Park.

title: Siri AI Still Not Enabled on HomePod Mini 2 With Latest Software Update
summary:

title: A breakthrough in magnetism could make AI chips use dramatically less energy
summary:
A promising new approach to building computer chips could dramatically reduce the energy needed for computing, including the rapidly growing demands of artificial intelligence.
Why Multiferroics Could Transform Computer ChipsWhat makes multiferroics so attractive for computing is the unusual connection between their electrical and magnetic properties.
Because the material's magnetic behavior is linked to its electrical polarization, the stored information can also be retrieved magnetically.
By preventing those fields from disrupting the material's electrical polarization, the additional layer addresses the other major cause of the dead layer effect.
These characteristics could help engineers build computer components that operate efficiently without the interference problems associated with conventional magnetic materials.
